orpheus-3b.model: Orpheus TTS 3B 0.1 fine-tuned (Canopy Labs), Unsloth ungated mirror

license.summary: Model card metadata: Apache-2.0 (both the Unsloth mirror and the official Canopy repo). The model is a fine-tune of meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, so the Llama 3.2 Community License also applies (Built with Llama attribution, Meta acceptable-use policy, 700M MAU clause). Canopy model card also forbids impersonation without consent, deception and fraudulent calls. SNAC codec: MIT. Orpheus-TTS code: Apache-2.0.

vram.llamacpp_q8_0: about 4.1 GB GPU total from llama.cpp buffer logs (weights 1530+1815 MiB, KV 224 MiB, compute 545 MiB, split over 2 GPUs) + CUDA context + SNAC; token embeddings 489 MiB stay in CPU RAM. nvidia-smi poll saw 1965 MiB on GPU 0 only.
vram.llamacpp_q4_k_m: about 2.7 GB GPU total from buffer logs (weights 859+1128 MiB, KV 224 MiB, compute 545 MiB) + context; nvidia-smi GPU 0: 1295 MiB.
vram.transformers_fp16: 7087 MiB nvidia-smi peak (torch max allocated 6664 MB).
vram.vllm_fp16: 12695 MiB nvidia-smi peak, but vLLM preallocates gpu_memory_utilization=0.80; real need is about 7 GB weights + KV.

problems: No path reaches real time on a T4. Best: llama.cpp Q4_K_M 63 audio tok/s (RTF 1.32), Q8_0 50 tok/s (RTF 1.64); transformers fp16 and vLLM fp16 about 23-24 tok/s (RTF 3.4-3.6). Real time needs about 82 tok/s, so streamed playback would underrun after the first chunk on a T4; a faster GPU (L4/A10/A100 class) or batching-friendly server is needed for live calls.

Kaggle's NvidiaTeslaT4 accelerator gave 2x T4. llama.cpp (default layer split) spread the model over both GPUs; for one stream the layers still run one after another, so speed should be close to a single T4, but this was not re-measured with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 (GPU budget).
llama-cpp-python 0.3.4 CUDA wheels exist only up to cp312; Kaggle runs Python 3.13, so run 1 skipped llama.cpp. Run 2 used the upstream v0.3.36-cu124 py3-none wheel (1.78 GB, 127 s to install).

vLLM 0.11.0 crashed with transformers 5.x (TokenizersBackend has no attribute all_special_tokens_extended); fixed in run 2 by pinning transformers==4.56.2. On Turing vLLM uses FlexAttention, piecewise CUDA graphs only and PyTorch top-p/top-k sampling (no FlashInfer), so it was no faster than plain transformers on the T4. Engine start 82 s (torch.compile 28 s).

Timings are sequential: the in-loop streaming SNAC decode (every 7 codes) blocks llama.cpp/transformers token generation; a production server would overlap it. Full-decode cost is small (0.03-0.07 s per clip).

Sampling (temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 50, repetition_penalty 1.1) makes length and delivery vary between paths for the same line (e.g. line 1 tara: 9.3 s Q8, 12.4 s Q4, 9.6 s transformers, 10.0 s vLLM).

We cannot listen. Canopy documents the 8 tags as emotive cues the fine-tuned voices perform; a CPU-only check (Whisper base.en transcript + AudioSet AST event classifier) is in events (see events_check).
orpheus-3b.primary_inference: llama.cpp via llama-cpp-python 0.3.36 (CUDA, all layers on GPU), GGUF orpheus-3b-0.1-ft-Q8_0.gguf

problems: dia_anchor_prompt condition skipped to stay inside the GPU budget
notes: README: tags 'will be recognized, but might result in unexpected output'; use them sparingly; unlisted tags may cause artifacts.
README: input under ~5 s of audio sounds unnatural, over ~20 s gets unnaturally fast; always start with [S1] and alternate speakers.
README: the model is not fine-tuned on a voice, so each run picks a new voice unless an audio prompt is given or the seed is fixed.
README: audio prompt should be 5-10 s, with its transcript placed before the text to generate; output contains only the new text.

Timings: gen_s is wall time of Dia.generate() (text encoder + prompt prefill + decode loop + DAC decode), CUDA-synchronised; RTF = gen_s / audio_s (below 1 = faster than real time). Non-streaming API: the caller waits gen_s before any audio.
